title: The Bicycle Powered by Applause
premise: A kinetic team needs the audience to clap in an exact impossible rhythm.
pressure: A human-powered sculpture moves only when the crowd claps in a rhythm no conductor can hold. The exhausted riders are thinking of withdrawing.
investigate: Count the missing beat using the crew's own pedals
success: The rhythm proves to be a message spelling a street name on the future race route.
failure: Your count slips, but a drummer writes the sequence on a discarded bib.
help: Teach the crowd an easier shared rhythm
helpOutcome: Children and mechanics clap together; the sculpture crosses the starting line without hurting anyone.

title: Glorious Competitor Number Minus One
premise: An unregistered sculpture was in every historic starting photo.
pressure: A sculpture numbered minus one appears in race photographs taken years before its maker was born. Officials want to erase the pictures to fix the record. The volunteer archivist would rather label what nobody understands.
investigate: Compare negatives, registration books and paint details without adding a convenient inventor
success: Across three decades the same tiny repair crew stands behind the vehicle. Their faces are indistinct; their tools and homemade badge are not.
failure: The copied registration numbers run together in the scanner. A retired mechanic still recognizes the paint, and asks you to preserve the original print.
help: Invite the maker and retired volunteers to describe only what they actually know
helpOutcome: The competitor gets a place to start, not a fabricated biography. The archive adds a small card reading ORIGIN UNVERIFIED.

title: The Engineering Judge from Elsewhere
premise: A judge gives perfect scores for violating Earth's physics.
pressure: A judge gives perfect marks to sculptures that ignore gravity. The ordinary builders object because their wheels, unlike everyone else's, must still touch the road. The judge insists the rubric is clear and refuses to show it.
investigate: Ask for one measurable criterion and insist it applies to every entrant
success: The scoring sheet predicts a loose wheel at the bay crossing. The crew checks the axle first; the judge gives them no points for avoiding disaster.
failure: The judge's demonstration leaves neither tracks nor witnesses. You record the failed test instead of awarding it the benefit of a supernatural doubt.
help: Help the competitors draft fair judging rules that can survive an absurd race
helpOutcome: The organizers publish rules rewarding practical ingenuity and crew safety. The impossible vehicles remain welcome, but no longer exempt from explaining themselves.

title: The Racer Who Is a Whole Committee
premise: Six people insist they are one entrant, and somehow all are correct.
pressure: Six racers insist they are one competitor. Their sculpture works only when all six pull separate controls in exact disagreement.
investigate: Inspect the machine's unusual linkage
success: The pedals are connected across an impossible gap, with an older race's number painted beneath.
failure: The test splits the chain; each rider still gives a coherent account of the same turn.
help: Help the crew enter as a team without forcing one identity
helpOutcome: Officials accept a shared entry, and the six choose their own order on the podium.

title: The Noon Siren at Midnight
premise: The race launches at noon, midnight and both at once.
pressure: The noon siren sounds at midnight and again at noon; both crowds appear in the same Plaza without seeing one another.
investigate: Compare recordings from both launches
success: A single whistle note has two timestamps and reveals a route into the missing harbor.
failure: Your recorder overloads but leaves the sound of a second crowd cheering.
help: Help marshals separate the overlapping starting lines
helpOutcome: The teams start safely, whatever the clocks claim.

title: Deadman's Drop, Then Up Again
premise: A kinetic sculpture rolls downhill so vigorously it reaches yesterday.
pressure: A sculpture descends Dead Man's Drop so fast its crew arrives yesterday. The racers' goggles still hold sand from today.
investigate: Check wheel marks against the dune's old track
success: The tire pattern is imprinted beneath a layer laid down before the sculpture was built.
failure: Wind erases the marks, but a racer brings back a lost glove they have not yet worn.
help: Help the crew rejoin the present race
helpOutcome: Volunteers anchor the sculpture and keep the riders from trying the descent again.

title: Sand Castle with a Mayor
premise: A miniature government attempts to reroute the race.
pressure: A sandcastle mayor declares the dune sovereign territory and charges the kinetic racers a border toll in seashells.
investigate: Ask how the tiny government protects the dune
success: The mayor's survey reveals a real patch of fragile vegetation beside the course.
failure: A wave knocks down city hall, leaving only the hand-lettered bylaw.
help: Help racers reroute around the castle and habitat
helpOutcome: Everyone earns a passage stamp without trampling the plants.

title: The Dune that Swallowed the Map
premise: A traveling dune relocates three of the player's remembered destinations.
pressure: A traveling dune swallows the course map and relocates three remembered destinations. A mechanic insists their team's finish line is now somewhere else.
investigate: Cross-check landmarks with a second route scout
success: The dune exposes an older road alignment that can guide the racers back safely.
failure: The skyline shifts before you make the last mark, leaving only a trustworthy bearing.
help: Help the teams make a public safe-route plan
helpOutcome: Crews agree on a visible path rather than follow contradictory private maps.

title: The Bribe That Bribes Itself
premise: A customary race bribe becomes sentient and offers a better deal.
pressure: A ceremonial race bribe becomes sentient and offers a much better deal: in exchange for applause, it will solve tomorrow's unfair judgment.
investigate: Read the offer out loud where everyone can hear it
success: The contract's fine print names a judge who has not arrived and a secret ballot.
failure: The bribe escapes under a sculpture, but your copy shows its signature is a tiny handprint.
help: Suggest an open award instead of another favor
helpOutcome: Racers create a mutual-help prize with transparent votes and no mysterious debt.

title: The Official Unofficial Rescue Team
premise: A crew of cryptids performs cheerful and competent roadside repairs.
pressure: A cheerful cryptid rescue crew repairs stalled vehicles using ordinary tools and occasionally impossible hands. A sponsor wants exclusive rights to photograph them.
investigate: Watch the crew work and document the mechanical fix
success: A patched axle bears the same strange maker's mark as the unknown racer.
failure: Their best mechanic slips away before questions, leaving a perfectly safe repair.
help: Help shield the rescuers from intrusive publicity
helpOutcome: The teams thank them with food and leave the rescue workers unnamed.

title: A Floating Sculpture with Opinions
premise: The craft refuses to float until its design philosophy is heard.
pressure: A floating sculpture refuses to launch until its makers acknowledge that a boat can be art and still have a duty to float.
investigate: Inspect the hull while listening to the machine
success: An extra compartment holds a chart showing a second water crossing beneath the bay.
failure: Your test wets the spectators and the craft remains stubbornly at the dock.
help: Let the team redesign without humiliating the artist
helpOutcome: The crew adds flotation and keeps the sculpture's outrageous silhouette intact.

title: The Second Water Crossing
premise: A mirror bay exists briefly just beneath the first.
pressure: Just below Humboldt Bay a mirror crossing becomes visible. One team sees an empty route; another sees the racers who disappeared yesterday.
investigate: Compare soundings from the real and mirror channels
success: The mirrored buoys spell out the date of a future public rescue drill.
failure: The reflection vanishes before the pole touches it; a skipper confirms it was not a trick of glare.
help: Keep the racers in the marked, supervised channel
helpOutcome: The race crosses safely while observers preserve the impossible sighting.

title: The Cosmic Coast Guard
premise: A rescue boat has paperwork from a galaxy that no longer exists.
pressure: A rescue boat flies a coast-guard insignia from a galaxy that no longer exists. Its crew demand forms nobody on Earth can sign.
investigate: Ask to inspect the rescue log before trusting the vessel
success: It lists a missing boat by a name not yet registered in the county.
failure: The crew salute and depart before producing credentials; their wake flows uphill.
help: Coordinate a real rescue with local volunteers
helpOutcome: The unknown sailors join the effort without commanding anyone to surrender their judgment.

title: The Tide Swaps Places with Time
premise: The protagonist can save equipment or rescue a stranger's memory.
pressure: For one minute the tide and time exchange places. A stranger begs for a lost memory while the crew's vital equipment begins to sink.
investigate: Chart the strange current to recover the equipment safely
success: You save the gear and discover an inscription that dates the flood one year ahead.
failure: The current steals the map as well as the rope. Everyone stays above water.
help: Help the stranger recover what matters before the tide turns
helpOutcome: They remember the face of someone they love, and the crew shares tools to replace what was lost.

title: The Race Officials' Secret Ballot
premise: Judges quietly decide which version of the county survives.
pressure: Race officials admit they have ballots for six versions of the county. Each version would make a different crew's sacrifice invisible.
investigate: Check who wrote the ballots and which actions are recorded
success: The tally includes verifiable deeds from your journey rather than a prediction about your beliefs.
failure: A sealed box vanishes before counting, but the officials agree the people affected must speak.
help: Demand a public account of costs before any vote
helpOutcome: The judges publish the competing proposals and leave the final choice to those who will live there.

title: The Trophy with a Pulse
premise: A trophy congratulates winners and whispers the county's original name.
pressure: A trophy beats with a pulse and whispers a forgotten county name. The winners fear that accepting it will erase their shared effort.
investigate: Listen to the rhythm and compare historical names
success: The pulse matches the interval between two future public meetings.
failure: You hear a name no map confirms; the trophy falls silent when polished.
help: Ask the crew what winning should mean
helpOutcome: They dedicate the prize to the people who kept the course open.

title: The Finish Line Moves
premise: A finish banner vanishes whenever someone claims to have solved the mystery.
pressure: The finish banner moves whenever somebody says the county's mystery is solved. Racers are exhausted and a child has been waiting at the supposed line.
investigate: Test the banner with a question instead of a declaration
success: It stops shifting beside a signpost marking the original road into town.
failure: It retreats another block, but you learn which promise makes it move.
help: Set a safe finish line people can actually reach
helpOutcome: A volunteer holds a simple ribbon. Every team finishes, even without an explanation.

title: The Ghost of Hobart's Contraption
premise: A legendary mechanical inspiration requests one final impossible modification.
pressure: A ghostly engineer appears beside a kinetic contraption and asks for one change that would make the machine impossible and strangely humane.
investigate: Ask the apparition to explain the actual mechanism
success: Its diagrams reveal a way to share effort between riders rather than stealing power from one.
failure: The drawing folds itself into dust, but a mechanic remembers the crucial hinge.
help: Help the tired riders finish their own design
helpOutcome: The ghost gives a quiet nod as the team repairs the bike without sacrificing safety.

title: Every Version of the Winner
premise: Five parallel champions arrive, all insisting they already met the player.
pressure: Five champions arrive, each wearing a different medal and remembering you differently. One praises you for an act you did not perform.
investigate: Check the awards against your own written log
success: You find the version whose claimed help actually appears in your notes; the rest accept correction.
failure: The medals exchange owners too quickly to trace, but nobody can take your witness account away.
help: Let the champions celebrate without erasing each other
helpOutcome: They share the stage and acknowledge the unseen crews who made every race possible.

title: The County Finally Votes
premise: The player's relationships, evidence and choices determine the surviving ending.
pressure: A county ballot lists wilderness, industry, spectacle and shared stewardship as if each were one neat box. Its clerk says your weekend's deeds will count more than your speech.
investigate: Review the ledger of actions before a final count
success: The ledger corrects an inflated claim and preserves a real promise that deserves to survive the vote.
failure: A page goes missing, but someone you helped testifies about what truly happened.
help: Insist the affected communities can speak before the future resolves
helpOutcome: The meeting reconvenes with open minutes. The actual fate remains to be decided by the journey's final reckoning.
